concepts.def: Russian chemist who arranged elements and left gaps.
A column in the table; same outer electrons.
A row in the table; same number of shells.
Group 1: soft, reactive metals like Na and K.
Group 7: reactive non-metals like Cl, Br, I.
Group 0: full outer shell, very unreactive.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1869 Mendeleev arranged the known elements by mass and properties.

His big idea: leave gaps for elements not yet discovered, and predict their properties. When gallium and germanium were found, they matched his predictions almost perfectly.

Today's table is ordered by atomic number, not mass.

Columns are groups. Elements in the same group have the same number of outer electrons and behave similarly.

Rows are periods. Elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells. Metals sit on the left, non-metals on the right.

Group 1 — alkali metals: lithium, sodium, potassium. Soft, very reactive, react with water to give hydrogen and an alkali.

Group 7 — halogens: fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine. Coloured non-metals that form salts. Group 0 — noble gases: helium, neon, argon. Almost no reactions.
